activePath.name: bluetooth-switch-0x30-body
activePath.selectedBy: upstream HMController.SubmitState early-returns into SwitchProPacker.BuildBody for 057E:2009 and never reaches the descriptor-driven builder; driver.c's Switch lane reads the body slices directly and synthesizes the 0x3F frame itself pre-handshake
activePath.reportSelectionReason: The driver decides the lane, not descriptor derivability. driver.c reads Data[2..10] always and Data[12..47] when IMU streaming is armed and DataSize >= 48; an 11-byte 0x3F submission passes the DataSize >= 11 guard and is silently misparsed as this body. An earlier revision of this contract froze the 0x3F report on the derivability argument; that lane was wrong and is retracted.
activePath.handshakeOwnership: The 0x80/0x01 request-reply machine and the fabricated SPI calibration image are entirely the driver's (SwitchHandle* in driver.c); the SDK submits state and nothing else.
activePath.profileExtendedReportPresentNote: switch-pro.json declares no extendedReport block at all.

report.framedByDriverAs: report 0x30 post-handshake (0x3F pre-handshake), with the driver's own frame counter, battery and vibrator overlay on bytes 0, 1 and 11
report.declaredProfileInputReportSizeNote: 362 is a REPORT LENGTH: this descriptor declares reports 0x31/0x32/0x33 at 361 data bytes plus a report ID. It is not the length of anything this candidate submits; the submission is the 48-byte 0x30 body with DataSize = 48.

stateKeySemantics.rule: HMAxis members are named after HID usages, but the host state mapper populates ONE fixed physical assignment shaped by the DualSense descriptor. Every axis here is bound by PHYSICAL SEMANTIC: Z/Rz are the right stick, Rx/Ry are the triggers.

axes.wireFormula: raw = 0x800 + truncate_toward_zero((clamp(value,0,1) * 2 - 1) * 0x600), clamped to [0, 0xFFF]; Y negates the centred value first because the wire is up-positive while HMAxis.Y/Rz are HID-style down-positive
axes.packing: 12-bit little-nibble pairs, the exact inverse of SDL's extraction: b0 = x & 0xFF; b1 = (x >> 8) | ((y & 0xF) << 4); b2 = y >> 4. wireByte below is the pair's base offset: X occupies base and the low nibble of base+1, Y the high nibble of base+1 and base+2.
axes.missingAxisReason: Consistent with the other personas' unsigned-axis default; a missing stick axis encodes the calibrated minimum rail 0x200 (0xE00 after Y inversion), not the neutral centre.
axes.calibration: centre 0x800, rails 0x200/0xE00 — the fabricated factory calibration the driver serves from SPI 0x603D, so a neutral stick packs to 00 08 80, byte-identical to the driver's own neutral prefill

hat.encoding: not a HID hat field: four plain d-pad bits in the left button byte (bit0=Down bit1=Up bit2=Right bit3=Left); each HMHat octant decomposes into its bit pair and wireValue is the resulting nibble mask
hat.nullStateRule: HMHat.None decomposes to no bits: the nibble is 0.

buttons.mapSource: semantic HMButton meanings bound to SDL HandleFullControllerState wire positions (the client under test), faces positional
buttons.divergenceFromUpstreamCaller: Upstream's HMController passes the raw HMButton bit mask into SwitchProPacker, which indexes it by the profile's layout button indices; with the raw mask those numberings disagree above the bumpers, so upstream lands HMButton.Back on ZL, Start on ZR, LeftStick on Minus, RightStick on Plus, Guide on LStick and Share on Home. No upstream test or doc states whether the consumer was meant to pre-convert. This host's StateMapper populates HMButton semantically, so this contract binds each semantic button to the wire position SDL documents for it. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, recorded; settle on hardware by pressing minus/plus/home and reading what a client reports.
